summary: Three kinds of things are forbidden for a nazir: becoming tamei, shaving, and anything from the grapevine. The mishnah teaches how much he must eat or drink to be punished.

chunks.en: Three kinds of things are forbidden for a nazir:
chunks.st: Three types of actions are prohibited for a nazirite:

chunks.en: becoming tamei, shaving, and anything that comes from the grapevine.
chunks.st: The contraction of ritual impurity from a corpse, and the shaving of one’s hair, and eating or drinking any substances that emerge from the vine.

chunks.en: All things that come from the grapevine
chunks.st: The mishna adds: And all products that emerge from the vine

chunks.en: join together with each other.
chunks.explain: Together they can make up the amount that brings malkus.
chunks.st: combine with one another
chunks.stMore: to the amount that renders a nazirite liable to receive lashes.

chunks.en: He is not punished until he eats
chunks.st: And he is liable only if he eats

words.note: Liable: he gets malkus, lashes from the Beis Din.

chunks.en: a kezayis of grapes.
chunks.st: an olive-bulk of the grapes.

words.note: About the size of an olive.

chunks.en: The first version of the mishnah said:
chunks.st: An initial version of the mishna says that a nazirite is liable to receive lashes

chunks.en: not until he drinks a revi'is of wine.
chunks.st: only if he drinks a quarter-log of wine.

words.note: A small amount, about a small cup.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: even if he soaked his bread in wine,
chunks.st: Even if he soaked his bread in wine

chunks.en: and together there is enough to make a kezayis,
chunks.st: and the two together contain enough to combine to the amount of an olive-bulk,

chunks.en: he is punished.
chunks.st: he is liable.

summary: A nazir is punished separately for wine, grapes, chartzanim and zagim. The Tannaim argue which are the skins and which are the seeds.

chunks.en: He is punished for wine by itself,
chunks.st: And furthermore, a nazirite is liable to receive lashes for consuming wine by itself,

chunks.en: and for grapes by themselves,
chunks.st: and for grapes by themselves,

chunks.en: and for chartzanim by themselves,
chunks.st: and for ḥartzannim by themselves,

chunks.en: and for zagim by themselves.
chunks.explain: Chartzanim and zagim are the skins and the seeds of grapes.
chunks.st: and for zaggim by themselves,
chunks.stMore: as each of these is forbidden separately by the Torah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: he is not punished until he eats
chunks.st: He is liable only if he eats

chunks.en: two chartzanim and one zag.
chunks.st: an olive-bulk that includes at least two ḥartzannim and one zag,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the verse “From ḥartzannim to zag” (Numbers 6:4), where the first term is in the plural and the second in the singular.

chunks.he: אֵלּוּ הֵן חַרְצַנִּים וְאֵלּוּ הֵן זַגִּים,
chunks.en: Which are chartzanim and which are zagim?
chunks.st: The mishna discusses the meaning of these terms: Which parts are ḥartzannim and which are zaggim?

chunks.en: The chartzanim are the outside parts,
chunks.st: The ḥartzannim are the outside parts, the skin of the grape,

chunks.en: the zagim are the inside parts.
chunks.st: while the zaggim are the inner parts, the seeds.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says it is the other way.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: So that you don't get mixed up,
chunks.st: The opposite is the case and this is the mnemonic so that you should not err:

chunks.en: it is like the bell of an animal:
chunks.st: It is like a bell [zog] worn by an animal,

chunks.en: the outside is the zog, and the inside is the clapper.
chunks.explain: So the zagim are the skins, on the outside.
chunks.st: in which the outer part, which corresponds to the skin of a grape, is called zog, and the inner portion of the bell, the clapper, which corresponds to the seeds in a grape, is called inbal.

summary: If a nazir shaves even a little hair, he is punished. He may wash his hair and separate it with his fingers, but he may not comb it.

chunks.en: Plain nezirus is thirty days.
chunks.st: A naziriteship of unspecified length lasts for thirty days.

chunks.en: If he shaved, or robbers shaved him,
chunks.st: If a nazirite shaved his hair during that period, or if he was shaved by bandits [listim] against his will,

chunks.en: it undoes thirty days.
chunks.st: this negates thirty days of his naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: which he must count afresh.

chunks.en: A nazir who shaved,
chunks.st: With regard to a nazirite who shaved his hair,

chunks.en: whether with scissors or with a razor,
chunks.st: whether he did so with scissors or with a razor,

chunks.en: or pulled out even a tiny bit, is punished.
chunks.st: or if he pulled out [sifsef ] any amount, he is liable.

chunks.en: A nazir may wash his hair and separate it with his fingers,
chunks.st: A nazirite may shampoo [ḥofef ] his head and separate [mefaspes]
chunks.stMore: his hairs manually, without concern that hairs might fall out.

chunks.en: but he may not comb it.
chunks.st: However, he may not comb his hair.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says: A nazirite

chunks.en: he may not wash his hair with earth,
chunks.st: may not shampoo his hair with earth

chunks.en: because it makes the hair fall out.
chunks.st: because this causes the hair to fall out.

summary: If a nazir keeps drinking wine all day, he gets malkus only once. If they warn him again and again, he gets malkus for each time. The same is true for shaving and for becoming tamei.

chunks.he: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן כָּל הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: A nazir who was drinking wine all day
chunks.st: A nazirite who was drinking wine all day

chunks.en: gets malkus only once.
chunks.st: is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה אַל תִּשְׁתֶּה,
chunks.en: If they told him, "Don't drink! Don't drink!"
chunks.st: If people said to him during the course of the day: Do not drink, do not drink,

chunks.en: and he drinks,
chunks.st: and nevertheless he continues to drink,

chunks.en: he gets malkus for each time.
chunks.explain: Each warning counts on its own.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time he was warned.

chunks.en: If he kept shaving all day,
chunks.st: If a nazirite kept shaving all day,

chunks.en: he gets malkus only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ אַל תְּגַלֵּחַ,
chunks.en: If they told him, "Don't shave! Don't shave!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not shave, do not shave,

chunks.en: and he shaves,
chunks.st: and he shaves,

chunks.en: he gets malkus for each time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time he was warned.

chunks.en: If he kept becoming tamei from dead people all day,
chunks.st: If he became ritually impure from a corpse many times all day,

chunks.en: he gets malkus only once.
chunks.st: he is liable to receive only one set of lashes.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לוֹ אַל תִּטַּמָּא אַל תִּטַּמָּא,
chunks.en: If they told him, "Don't become tamei! Don't become tamei!"
chunks.st: If they said to him: Do not become impure, do not become impure,

chunks.en: and he becomes tamei,
chunks.st: and he continues to become impure,

chunks.en: he gets malkus for each time.
chunks.st: he is liable for each and every time he was warned.

summary: Each of the three things forbidden to a nazir is stricter in some way. Tumah and shaving undo his days, things from the grapevine are never allowed, and tumah is stricter than shaving.

chunks.en: Three kinds of things are forbidden for a nazir:
chunks.st: Three types of actions are prohibited for a nazirite:

chunks.en: becoming tamei, shaving, and anything that comes from the grapevine.
chunks.st: Contracting ritual impurity imparted by a corpse, and shaving his hair, and eating or drinking any substances that emerge from the vine.

chunks.he: חֹמֶר בַּטֻּמְאָה וּבַתִּגְלַחַת מִבַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן,
chunks.en: Tumah and shaving are stricter than things from the grapevine,
chunks.st: There is a greater stricture with regard to the prohibitions of impurity and shaving than that of substances that emerge from the vine,

chunks.en: because tumah and shaving undo his days,
chunks.st: as impurity and shaving negate his naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he must add thirty days to his term of naziriteship or start it afresh.

chunks.en: but things from the grapevine do not undo them.
chunks.st: But if he eats or drinks that which emerges from the vine, this does not negate his naziriteship.

chunks.he: חֹמֶר בַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן מִבַּטֻּמְאָה וּבַתִּגְלַחַת,
chunks.en: Things from the grapevine are stricter than tumah and shaving,
chunks.st: Conversely, there is a greater stricture with regard to substances that emerge from the vine than with regard to impurity and shaving,

chunks.he: שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן לֹא הֻתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ,
chunks.en: because things from the grapevine are never allowed,
chunks.st: as in the case of products that emerge from the vine nothing is exempted from its general prohibition
chunks.stMore: in certain circumstances, i.e., there are no exceptions.

chunks.en: but tumah and shaving are sometimes allowed:
chunks.st: But with regard to impurity and shaving certain cases are exempted from their general prohibition.

chunks.en: for shaving that is a mitzvah, and for a mes mitzvah.
chunks.explain: A mes mitzvah is a dead person with nobody else to bury him.
chunks.st: For example, there are the cases of obligatory shaving, e.g., a leper who was purified during his naziriteship, and of a corpse with no one to bury it [met mitzva].
chunks.stMore: A nazirite may tend to the burial of a met mitzva, despite the fact that he will thereby contract ritual impurity from a corpse.

words.en: and for a dead person of

chunks.en: And tumah is stricter than shaving,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: And there is a greater stricture with regard to impurity than with regard to shaving, as a nazirite’s

chunks.en: because tumah undoes everything,
chunks.st: impurity negates all
chunks.stMore: his days of naziriteship and begins his term afresh,

chunks.en: and he must bring a korban for it,
chunks.st: and he is liable to bring an offering for it, before starting his new term of naziriteship.

chunks.he: וְתִגְלַחַת אֵינָהּ סוֹתֶרֶת אֶלָּא שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם
chunks.en: but shaving undoes only thirty days,
chunks.st: But shaving negates only thirty days at most,

chunks.en: and he does not bring a korban for it.
chunks.st: and he is not liable to bring an offering for it.

summary: A nazir who became tamei is sprinkled on the third and seventh days, shaves on the seventh, and brings his korbanos on the eighth. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Tarfon discuss how he is different from a metzora.

chunks.en: How is the shaving of tumah done?
chunks.st: With regard to the shaving of ritual impurity performed by a nazirite who became impure during his naziriteship, how is it performed?

chunks.en: The Kohen would sprinkle him on the third and the seventh days,
chunks.explain: He was sprinkled with the special water that makes people tahor.
chunks.st: The priest would sprinkle the waters of purification on him on the third and the seventh
chunks.stMore: days after he contracted his impurity, as performed for all those who contracted impurity imparted by a corpse.

chunks.en: and he shaves on the seventh,
chunks.st: And he shaves his hair on the seventh day

chunks.en: and brings his korbanos on the eighth.
chunks.st: and brings his offerings on the eighth day.

chunks.en: And if he shaved on the eighth,
chunks.st: And if he shaved on the eighth day

chunks.en: he brings his korbanos on that same day.
chunks.st: he brings his offerings on that day, this is

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon said to him:

chunks.en: "What is the difference between this one and a metzora?"
chunks.explain: A metzora who shaves on the eighth brings his korbanos on the ninth.
chunks.st: What is the difference between this ritual and that of a leper?
chunks.stMore: A leper also shaves on the seventh day and sacrifices his offerings on the eighth. However, if a leper shaves on the eighth day he brings his offerings on the ninth day, not on the day of his shaving.

words.note: A person with tzaraas, a skin sickness from the Torah.

chunks.en: He answered him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to him:

chunks.en: "This one becomes tahor through his days,
chunks.explain: He is already tahor from the seventh day.
chunks.st: The purification of this impure nazirite depends on his days,
chunks.stMore: as he immerses on the seventh day like all those who contract impurity imparted by a corpse, which means he is already ritually pure on the eighth day.

chunks.en: but a metzora becomes tahor through his shaving,
chunks.st: But with regard to a leper, his purification depends on his shaving.
chunks.stMore: Any immersion performed earlier is of no account, and must be repeated.

chunks.en: and he does not bring his korban
chunks.st: And a leper brings his offering

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיָה מְעֹרַב שָׁמֶשׁ:
chunks.en: unless the sun has set for him."
chunks.st: only if the sun has set
chunks.stMore: following his immersion. Since offerings are not sacrificed at night, the bringing of his offering is postponed until the following day.

summary: At the end of his nezirus, a tahor nazir brings three animals and shaves his hair. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Elazar argue after which korban he shaves.

chunks.en: How is the shaving of taharah done?
chunks.st: With regard to a nazirite’s shaving of purity after the completion of his term of naziriteship, how is it performed?

chunks.en: He would bring three animals:
chunks.st: He would bring three animals:

chunks.en: a chatas, an olah, and shelamim.
chunks.st: One for a sin-offering, one for a burnt-offering, and one for a peace-offering.

chunks.en: He shechts the shelamim
chunks.st: And he slaughters the peace-offering

chunks.en: and shaves after them.
chunks.st: and shaves his hair after he slaughters them.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yehudah.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה מְגַלֵּחַ אֶלָּא עַל הַחַטָּאת,
chunks.en: he would shave only after the chatas,
chunks.st: He would shave only after he slaughtered the sin-offering,

chunks.en: because the chatas always comes first.
chunks.st: as the sin-offering precedes the other offerings in all places,
chunks.stMore: and therefore he sacrifices the sin-offering first. He shaves his hair after he slaughters this offering.

chunks.he: וְאִם גִּלַּח עַל אַחַת מִשְּׁלָשְׁתָּן, יָצָא:
chunks.en: And if he shaved after any one of the three, it counts.
chunks.st: And if he shaved after the sacrifice of any one of the three of them, he has fulfilled his obligation after the fact.

summary: A nazir who brought three animals without saying which is which uses each for the korban it fits. After the shaving of taharah, he throws his hair into the fire under the pot of his shelamim.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: If he brought three animals and did not say which is for which korban,
chunks.st: If a nazirite brought three animals without specifying which of them was for which offering,

chunks.en: the one that fits a chatas is brought as a chatas,
chunks.st: the one that is fit for a sin-offering, i.e., a female sheep in its first year, is sacrificed as a sin-offering;

chunks.en: the one that fits an olah is brought as an olah,
chunks.st: that which is fit for a burnt-offering, a male sheep in its first year, is sacrificed as a burnt-offering;

chunks.en: and the one that fits shelamim is brought as shelamim.
chunks.st: and that which is fit for a peace-offering, a ram, i.e., a male sheep over the age of one year, is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

chunks.en: He would take the hair of his nazir head
chunks.st: After the nazirite shaved off his hair, he would take the hair of his consecrated head

chunks.en: and throw it under the pot.
chunks.explain: The shelamim was cooking in the pot, so the hair burned in its fire.
chunks.st: and throw it under the pot
chunks.stMore: in which the peace-offering was cooked, where it would burn.

chunks.en: And if he shaved outside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: And if the nazirite shaved in the rest of the country, i.e., outside the Temple,

chunks.en: he would not throw it under the pot.
chunks.st: he would not throw the hair under the pot.
chunks.basisNote: Our Hebrew text has no "not" here; Steinsaltz and Bartenura both explain that he does not throw it.

chunks.en: When is this so?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: At the shaving of taharah.
chunks.st: It is said with regard to the shaving of purity.

chunks.en: But at the shaving of tumah,
chunks.st: However, with regard to the shaving of impurity,
chunks.stMore: i.e., shaving that accompanied his guilt-offering and sin-offering of birds after his term of naziriteship was interrupted by impurity,

chunks.en: he would not throw it under the pot.
chunks.st: he would not throw his hair under the pot
chunks.stMore: in which his offerings were cooked, as the Torah stated this requirement only for a pure nazirite.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: everyone throws it under the pot,
chunks.st: Everyone throws his hair under the pot,
chunks.stMore: including a pure nazirite who shaved outside the Temple and an impure nazirite,

chunks.en: except only a tamei nazir who shaved outside.
chunks.st: except for an impure nazirite who shaved in the rest of the country. In that case alone
chunks.stMore: he refrains from throwing his hair to be burned beneath his offering.

summary: The Kohen waves the cooked foreleg of the ram and two matzos on the nazir's hands, and then the nazir may drink wine again. Rabbi Shimon says he may already drink once the blood of one korban was sprinkled.

chunks.he: הָיָה מְבַשֵּׁל אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים אוֹ שׁוֹלְקָן.
chunks.en: He would cook the shelamim, or boil it well.
chunks.st: The nazirite would cook the peace-offering or overcook it, i.e., cook it thoroughly.

chunks.he: הַכֹּהֵן נוֹטֵל אֶת הַזְּרוֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה מִן הָאַיִל,
chunks.en: The Kohen takes the cooked foreleg of the ram,
chunks.st: The priest takes the cooked foreleg from the ram,

chunks.en: and one matzah loaf from the basket,
chunks.st: and one unleavened loaf from the basket,

chunks.en: and one matzah wafer,
chunks.st: and one unleavened wafer,

chunks.en: and puts them on the nazir's palms and waves them.
chunks.st: and places them on the palms of the nazirite and waves them, as described in the Torah (Numbers 6:19–20).

chunks.en: After that the nazir is allowed
chunks.st: And afterward the nazirite is permitted

chunks.en: to drink wine and to become tamei from dead people.
chunks.st: to drink wine and to contract ritual impurity imparted by a corpse.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים,
chunks.en: as soon as the blood of one korban is sprinkled for him,
chunks.st: Once the blood of one of the offerings has been sprinkled on the nazirite’s behalf,

chunks.he: הֻתַּר הַנָּזִיר לִשְׁתּוֹת בְּיַיִן וּלְהִטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים:
chunks.en: the nazir may drink wine and become tamei from dead people.
chunks.st: the nazirite is permitted to drink wine and to contract ritual impurity imparted by a corpse.
chunks.stMore: The rest of the ritual is not indispensable for his purification.

summary: If a nazir shaved after a korban that turned out to be pasul, his shaving does not count. Rabbi Shimon says that only that one korban does not count.
stIntro: As taught earlier (45a) the nazirite shaves after having brought one, or all, of his offerings. This mishna discusses what the halakha is if the offering was found to be invalid after the nazirite had shaved.

chunks.en: If he shaved after the korban, and it turned out to be pasul,
chunks.st: If a nazirite shaved based upon the requisite offering, and afterward the offering was found to be invalid for any reason,

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.en: If he shaved after a chatas that was brought not for its own sake,
chunks.explain: It was brought with the wrong korban in mind.
chunks.st: If he shaved based upon the sin-offering, that was found to have been sacrificed not for its own sake, which invalidates the offering,

chunks.en: and after that he brought his korbanos for their own sake,
chunks.st: and afterward he brought his other offerings for their own sake,

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his other offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.he: גִּלַּח עַל הָעוֹלָה אוֹ עַל הַשְּׁלָמִים
chunks.en: If he shaved after the olah or the shelamim
chunks.st: If he shaved based upon the requisite burnt-offering or having brought the requisite peace-offering,

chunks.en: that were brought not for their own sake,
chunks.st: and these were offered not for their own sake,

chunks.en: and after that he brought his korbanos for their own sake,
chunks.st: and afterward he brought his remaining offerings for their own sake,

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: In the case of one who shaved based upon a burnt-offering or a peace-offering that was sacrificed not for its own sake,

chunks.en: that korban does not count for him,
chunks.st: that offering, which was performed incorrectly, does not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation;

chunks.en: but his other korbanos do count.
chunks.st: however, his other offerings do count.

chunks.en: And if he shaved after all three,
chunks.st: And everyone agrees that if he shaved based upon all three of them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he brought all three offerings, without specifying which offering he is basing his shaving upon,

chunks.en: and even one of them turned out kosher,
chunks.st: and even one of them was found valid,

chunks.en: his shaving counts,
chunks.st: his shaving is valid,

chunks.en: and he must bring the other korbanos.
chunks.st: but he must bring the other offerings in order to fulfill his obligation.

summary: If a nazir became tamei after the blood of one of his korbanos was sprinkled, Rabbi Eliezer says he loses all his days. The Sages say he brings the rest of his korbanos, as happened with Miriam of Tarmod.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים
chunks.en: Someone for whom the blood of one korban was sprinkled,
chunks.st: With regard to one on whose behalf the blood of one of his nazirite offerings was sprinkled on the altar,

chunks.en: and then he became tamei:
chunks.st: and he became ritually impure before bringing the rest of his offerings,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it undoes everything.
chunks.st: His impurity negates the entire tally, and he remains a nazirite.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he brings the rest of his korbanos and becomes tahor.
chunks.st: Let him bring the rest of his offerings and be purified.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.en: There was a story with Miriam of Tarmod,
chunks.st: An incident occurred involving Miriam of Tarmod who was a nazirite,

chunks.en: that the blood of one of her korbanos was sprinkled for her,
chunks.st: that the blood of one of her offerings was sprinkled on her behalf,

chunks.en: and people came and told her
chunks.st: and they came and told her

chunks.en: that her daughter was very sick.
chunks.st: that her daughter was mortally ill.

chunks.en: She went and found that she had died.
chunks.st: And she went and found that her daughter was dead, and thereby contracted impurity.

chunks.en: And the Sages said,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis said:

chunks.en: "She should bring the rest of her korbanos and become tahor."
chunks.st: Let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified.
